# Lactase Activity – Replicate Plate Analysis

## Methods
Lactase activity (U/mL) was measured in 16 wells on each of three replicate plates
(plate_A, plate_B, plate_C). Plate means and the grand mean were computed across all
48 wells. Plate-to-plate agreement was assessed by comparing individual plate means to
the grand mean and by inspecting the coefficient of variation (CV).

## Results

| Plate   | n wells | Mean activity (U/mL) | SD (U/mL) |
|---------|---------|----------------------|-----------|
| plate_A | 16      | 12.33                | 0.72      |
| plate_B | 16      | 12.95                | 0.90      |
| plate_C | 16      | 12.56                | 0.82      |

**plate_A mean = 12.33**  
**plate_B mean = 12.95**  
**plate_C mean = 12.56**  
**Grand mean (all 48 wells) = 12.61**

## Plate Agreement
The three plate means span a range of 0.62 U/mL (12.33 – 12.95 U/mL), which
represents ~4.9 % of the grand mean. The between-plate CV is approximately 2.5 %,
well within the ≤ 15 % threshold commonly accepted for microplate assays. All three
plates therefore agree closely, and no plate shows a systematic outlier response.

## Conclusion
Mean lactase activity is consistent across the three replicate plates
(grand mean 12.61 U/mL). The modest plate-to-plate variation (CV ≈ 2.5 %) is
attributable to normal pipetting and thermal gradients and does not compromise data
quality.
